notes: Calpine closed on Jan 7, 2026. The purchase price was about $22B (the DOJ cites a $26.6B net purchase price), paid with 50M new CEG shares and about $4.5B in cash. Calpine adds about 23 GW of gas, geothermal, battery and solar capacity and a retail business serving about 62 TWh a year.

The DOJ required six plant sales (five in PJM, one in ERCOT) plus the Gregory interest. Gregory was sold in January 2026. The last required sale, Brazos Valley (606 MW, ERCOT), goes to LS Power for $860M, needs DOJ approval and is expected to close by the end of 2026.

Q2 revenue of $7.5B missed the ~$7.94B consensus, but adjusted EPS of $2.55 beat. Management credits Calpine accretion, higher PJM capacity prices and commercial margins, partly offset by nuclear outages.

Constellation signed about 920 MW of long-term nuclear PPAs in Q2. It says its fleet can add about 1,100 MW of uprates, including 900 MW that are possible with customer support, and the Google deal covers 890 MW of uprates.
Institutions hold about 83% of shares and insiders about 0.2% (StockAnalysis).

calls.text: Consensus Buy across 22 analysts; average target $341.53 (+14.6% vs the Oct 9 close)
BMO Capital: Outperform, PT $379 → $350 after the Amazon Calvert Cliffs deal (Oct 2, 2026)

catalysts.event: Google: a 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear capacity from uprates at 11 PJM units (Braidwood, Byron, LaSalle, Quad Cities, Limerick and Salem), with $4.3B+ of Constellation capex. The first uprate is due by 2028 and all of it by the end of 2032. A separate 15-year supply deal covers 2,700 MW from the existing PJM fleet (3,590 MW in total).
Amazon: a 20-year PPA for 690 MW from Calvert Cliffs (MD), including a ~190 MW uprate due online 2030–2032. It supports more than $3B of investment and relicensing.
Crane Clean Energy Center (former Three Mile Island Unit 1) restart: 835 MW sold to Microsoft under a 20-year PPA. The NRC fuel license and the FERC capacity-rights transfer were approved in Q2 2026.
Meta: a 20-year PPA for all of Clinton (IL), 1,121 MW after a 30 MW uprate, starts when the Illinois zero-emission credit support ends. It supports relicensing.
Q3 2026 earnings: the 2026 guide ($11.50–$12.50), Calpine integration and new data-center deals
Calpine: the Brazos Valley sale to LS Power ($860M), the last DOJ-required divestiture, awaits DOJ approval
PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement for data-center load: FERC accepted it but suspended it for five months on Sep 29, 2026, and set a paper hearing

Data-center power demand: the Google deal answers PJM's 'bring your own power' proposal for large loads. Management says FERC and PJM are opening new paths to connect large loads, and expects regulatory clarity in PJM in 2H 2026.
Lock-up ends on the remaining 25M of the 50M shares issued to Calpine's former owners (the first half was released Jun 30, 2026)

Federal nuclear PTC: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act kept the 45U credit for existing reactors through tax years starting before 2033 (adding foreign-entity rules). New nuclear and uprates can use the 45Y credit.

bull.text: Hyperscalers are paying for new nuclear output: Google (3,590 MW incl. 890 MW of uprates), Amazon (690 MW), Meta (1,121 MW) and Microsoft (835 MW from Crane)
Uprates add firm power faster than new plants: about 1,100 MW is identified, mostly backed by 20-year contracts
Calpine adds about 23 GW of gas and geothermal plus retail scale. The 2026 EPS guide was raised to $11.50–$12.50, and about $2.2B of buybacks were done by Q2.
The 45U nuclear PTC was kept through 2032, which puts a floor under existing-fleet economics

bear.text: PJM policy risk: FERC suspended the reliability backstop until Feb 2027, and shares closed −4.0% on Sep 30
Growth is mostly the acquisition: consensus sees revenue +38.9% this year but only +3.4% next year
Thin free cash flow ($295M TTM) against $24.7B of debt and heavy uprate and restart capex ($4.3B+ for Google alone)
Price targets are being cut (Scotiabank $441 → $355, BMO $379 → $350), leaving only ~14% upside to the average target

runContext.title: Why CEG left Growth's backups on Oct 7
runContext.summary: CEG was #15 on the Growth bench on Oct 6. The Oct 7 rescreen applied stricter written rules, and CEG failed two of them. It is not on any Futura list today.

points.label: Upside to target
points.note: Oct 6: $342.98 target vs $300.40 close; the rule needs 15%+ (Oct 7 close: +14.0%)

points.label: PEG
points.note: Now reported (n/a on Oct 6); the cap is 1.5

points.label: TTM revenue growth
points.note: Passes the 15% rule, but only because of Calpine

signals: The Oct 7 Growth rules require 15%+ upside to the average target. CEG was at +14.2% on the Oct 6 close the screen used.
They also require growth analysts expect to continue: consensus revenue growth of 8%+ next fiscal year. CEG's FY2027 consensus is +3.4%, because 2026's +38.9% is the one-time Calpine consolidation.
Its other inputs pass: $106B market cap, forward P/E ~24, Buy from 22 analysts, beta 1.13, share count +6.8% (under the 20% cap), and ample volume.
As of Oct 8 it still fails both rules, and its PEG of 1.55 is now just over the 1.5 cap. The Google deal (Oct 6) lifted the price 12%, but targets were cut at the same time.
runContext.caveat: The Oct 7 run didn't save a per-stock rejection log. The upside figure is from CEG's Oct 6 bench entry; the next-year growth and PEG are today's StockAnalysis consensus, checked against the same rules in the list's method text.
